# AlphaFold 3

This package provides an implementation of the inference pipeline of
AlphaFold 3. See below for how to access the model parameters. You may only use
AlphaFold 3 model parameters if received directly from Google. Use is subject to
these
[terms of use](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/main/WEIGHTS_TERMS_OF_USE.md).

Any publication that discloses findings arising from using this source code, the
model parameters or outputs produced by those should [cite](#citing-this-work)
the
[Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07487-w)
paper.

Please also refer to the Supplementary Information for a detailed description of
the method.

AlphaFold 3 is also available at
[alphafoldserver.com](https://alphafoldserver.com) for non-commercial use,
though with a more limited set of ligands and covalent modifications.

For commercial use, AlphaFold 3 is available via
[Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform on Google Cloud](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/open-models/alphafold-3).

If you have any questions, please contact the AlphaFold team at
[alphafold@google.com](mailto:alphafold@google.com).

## Obtaining Model Parameters

This repository contains all necessary code for AlphaFold 3 inference. You can
download the AlphaFold 3 model parameters from
https://storage.googleapis.com/alphafold3/af3.bin.zst. Use is subject to these
[terms of use](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3/blob/main/WEIGHTS_TERMS_OF_USE.md).

The model parameters for the SynthID Bio-structure version of AlphaFold 3, which
predicts watermarked structures, is available at
https://storage.googleapis.com/alphafold3/af3_synthid.bin.zst. See
[google-deepmind/synthidbio](https://github.com/google-deepmind/synthidbio) for
more details.

The model parameters for AlphaFold 3 Leaving Atom (AF3-LA) can be used as an
alternative model fine-tuned for leaving atom handling. The weights are
available at https://storage.googleapis.com/alphafold3/af3_leaving_atom.bin.zst
and are subject to the same terms of use as the original AlphaFold 3 model
parameters. See
[google-deepmind/alphaprotein-novo](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphaprotein-novo)
for more details.

## Installation and Running Your First Prediction

See the [installation documentation](docs/installation.md).

Once you have installed AlphaFold 3, you can test your setup using e.g. the
following input JSON file named `fold_input.json`:

```json
{
  "name": "2PV7",
  "sequences": [
    {
      "protein": {
        "id": ["A", "B"],
        "sequence": "GMRESYANENQFGFKTINSDIHKIVIVGGYGKLGGLFARYLRASGYPISILDREDWAVAESILANADVVIVSVPINLTLETIERLKPYLTENMLLADLTSVKREPLAKMLEVHTGAVLGLHPMFGADIASMAKQVVVRCDGRFPERYEWLLEQIQIWGAKIYQTNATEHDHNMTYIQALRHFSTFANGLHLSKQPINLANLLALSSPIYRLELAMIGRLFAQDAELYADIIMDKSENLAVIETLKQTYDEALTFFENNDRQGFIDAFHKVRDWFGDYSEQFLKESRQLLQQANDLKQG"
      }
    }
  ],
  "modelSeeds": [1],
  "dialect": "alphafold3",
  "version": 1
}
```

You can then run AlphaFold 3 using the following command:

```
docker run -it \
    --volume $HOME/af_input:/root/af_input \
    --volume $HOME/af_output:/root/af_output \
    --volume <MODEL_PARAMETERS_DIR>:/root/models \
    --volume <DATABASES_DIR>:/root/public_databases \
    --gpus all \
    alphafold3 \
    python run_alphafold.py \
    --json_path=/root/af_input/fold_input.json \
    --model_dir=/root/models \
    --output_dir=/root/af_output
```

There are various flags that you can pass to the `run_alphafold.py` command, to
list them all run `python run_alphafold.py --help`. Two fundamental flags that
control which parts AlphaFold 3 will run are:

*   `--run_data_pipeline` (defaults to `true`): whether to run the data
    pipeline, i.e. genetic and template search. This part is CPU-only, time
    consuming and could be run on a machine without a GPU.
*   `--run_inference` (defaults to `true`): whether to run the inference. This
    part requires a GPU.

## 是什么

BEER（Biophysical Evaluation Engine for Residues）是一个桌面应用程序，用于对蛋白质序列进行综合生物物理分析。它接受序列（粘贴、FASTA/PDB 导入或从 UniProt/RCSB 获取），按需运行 14 个经典分析模块和 24 个基于 ESMC BiLSTM 的 AI 预测头，并提供交互式出版级图表、3D 结构查看器和可导出的报告。它旨在替代多个在线服务器，提供一体化的本地分析工具。

## 亮点

- **一体化集成**：将经典生物物理计算（如疏水性、电荷、聚集倾向）与基于 ESM C 600M 蛋白语言模型的 AI 预测（如无序、结合位点、翻译后修饰）整合在单一 GUI 中，无需切换多个工具。
- **按需计算与缓存**：AI 预测头按需运行，且嵌入缓存，后续预测快速；经典分析无长度限制。
- **不确定性量化**：所有 AI 头支持 MC-Dropout 不确定性带（±1σ），提供预测置信度。
- **丰富的可视化**：交互式 3D 结构查看器（基于 Mol*），支持多种着色模式（如按 AI 预测轨道着色），并支持导出 PyMOL/ChimeraX 脚本。
- **可扩展的输入输出**：支持 FASTA、PDB、UniProt 获取、多链处理，输出多种格式（JSON、CSV、HTML、PNG/SVG/PDF）。
- **隐私与离线模式**：提供离线模式，阻止所有网络连接，保护序列隐私。
- **稳健的工程实现**：线程安全（ESMCEmbedder 使用 RLock 保护的缓存）、后台任务处理（如截断分析）、错误处理（如 macOS 上的 OpenMP 冲突）。

## 为何对本课题有用

BEER 直接针对 IDR/IDP 研究，其 AI 预测头包括无序区域预测（基于实验标签训练），并集成了多种与无序蛋白相关的经典指标（如 GRAVY、电荷、catGRANULE 分数、PLAAC 分数、LARKS 检测）。对于 IDR/IDP × LLPS × AI/模拟课题，BEER 提供了：

- **无序预测的基准**：其无序头基于 DisProt 实验标签训练，可作为 IDR 预测的参考或对比。
- **相分离相关特征**：catGRANULE 分数和 PLAAC 分数直接用于预测凝聚体形成倾向，可迁移到 LLPS 研究。
- **AI 预测框架**：ESMC 嵌入 + BiLSTM 头的架构可被借鉴，用于开发新的 IDR 相关预测器（如互作位点、修饰位点）。
- **不确定性量化方法**：MC-Dropout 的实现可迁移到其他预测模型，提供置信度评估。
- **数据集成模式**：从 UniProt、DisProt、PhaSepDB 等数据库获取注释的流程，可用于构建 IDR 相关数据集。

## 怎么用

- **安装**：需要 Python 3.10+，通过 `pip install .` 安装（依赖 PyTorch、ESM、PySide6 等）。GPU 加速需额外安装 CUDA 版 PyTorch。
- **主入口**：命令行运行 `beer` 启动 GUI；无头模式使用 `beer analyze` 命令，例如：
  ```bash
  beer analyze --sequence MADVFGKDMVNQ... --format json
  beer analyze --fasta my_protein.fasta --format html --output report.html
  beer analyze --accession P04637 --format tsv --no-esmc --output p53.tsv
  ```
- **输入格式**：序列字符串、FASTA 文件、PDB 文件、UniProt 或 PDB 数据库 ID。
- **输出格式**：JSON、CSV、TSV、HTML 报告；图表可导出为 PNG/SVG/PDF。
- **测试**：运行 `pytest` 执行测试套件（位于 `tests/` 目录），可用于调试和验证。
- **关键模块**：`beer/analysis/` 包含经典分析逻辑，`beer/embeddings/` 包含 ESMC 嵌入和 AI 头，`beer/gui/` 包含界面。

## 核心 idea

BEER 的核心方法学在于**将经典生物物理规则与蛋白语言模型嵌入相结合**，通过一个统一的界面提供多维度分析。其 AI 预测头采用 BiLSTM 架构，利用 ESM C 600M 的嵌入表示，针对每个任务（如无序、结合位点）训练专门的分类器，并引入 MC-Dropout 进行不确定性估计。这种“预训练嵌入 + 轻量任务头”的范式，使得在有限标注数据下也能获得较好的预测性能，同时支持按需计算和缓存，提高了实用性。

## 可搬移点

- **ESMC 嵌入模块**（`beer/embeddings/esmc_embedder.py`）：可解耦并用于自定义的 IDR 预测或互作建模 Pipeline，作为特征提取器。
- **MC-Dropout 不确定性实现**：可迁移到其他预测模型，提供置信度区间。
- **经典指标计算**（如 GRAVY、catGRANULE、PLAAC）：这些函数可直接复制或 import 到自定义脚本中，用于 IDR/LLPS 特征计算。
- **数据获取与注释逻辑**（UniProt、DisProt、PhaSepDB 集成）：可借鉴其 API 调用和数据处理流程，构建自己的数据集。
- **许可证**：源代码为 GPL v3，ESM C 模型为 MIT 许可。若需在闭源项目中使用，需注意 GPL 传染性；若仅借鉴思路，需确认。

**注意**：README 未提供具体函数接口或模块内部细节，以上可搬移点基于目录结构和描述推断，实际移植时需查看源码。

# BEER — Biophysical Evaluation Engine for Residues

**Website:** [https://chemgame.github.io/BEER](https://chemgame.github.io/BEER)

The AI predictions use the **ESM C 600M** protein language model (MIT licence, Chan Zuckerberg Biohub), downloaded automatically on first use.

**BEER** is a desktop application for integrated biophysical analysis of protein sequences. It accepts a sequence (pasted, imported as FASTA/PDB, or fetched from UniProt/RCSB), runs 14 classical analysis sections and 24 ESMC BiLSTM neural AI prediction heads on demand, and gives you interactive publication-quality graphs, a 3D structure viewer, and exportable per-section reports — all from a single GUI.

I built BEER because I wanted a single tool that handles everything from basic physicochemical properties to disorder prediction, aggregation hotspots, RNA-binding propensity, and phase separation metrics, without jumping between half a dozen web servers.

> **If you use BEER in your research, please cite:**
> Mukherjee, S. *arXiv*:2504.20561. DOI: [https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2504.20561](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.20561)

<details>
<summary>BibTeX</summary>

```bibtex

  author    = {Mukherjee, Saumyak},
  title     = {{BEER}: Biophysical Evaluation Engine for Residues},

  url       = {https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.20561},

```

</details>

---

## Installation

**Requirements:** Python 3.10 or later · macOS, Windows, or Linux · ~3 GB disk space
(PyTorch + the ESMC backbone; the 490 MB head weights download on first AI use)

A single install pulls everything — the AI prediction heads (PyTorch + ESMC) and
the 3D structure viewer are core features, not optional add-ons:

```bash
conda create -n beer python=3.12 -y
conda activate beer
git clone https://github.com/chemgame/BEER.git
cd BEER
pip install .
```

That's it — `beer` now has the full AI + visualization feature set. The default
pulls a CPU build of PyTorch. **For GPU acceleration (CUDA 12.1)**, replace torch
with a CUDA build afterward:

```bash
pip install "torch>=2.0" --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121 --force-reinstall
```

**Development install** (editable, changes to source take effect immediately):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/chemgame/BEER.git && cd BEER
pip install -e ".[dev]"
```

**Linux only** — Qt requires xcb platform libraries. Choose the method that fits your system:

**With root access — Ubuntu / Debian:**
```bash
sudo apt-get install -y \
    libxcb-cursor0 libxcb-icccm4 libxcb-image0 libxcb-keysyms1 \
    libxcb-render-util0 libxcb-xkb1 libxkbcommon-x11-0 \
    libnss3 libxcomposite1 libxrandr2 libxdamage1 libdrm2 libgbm1
```

**With root access — Fedora / RHEL:**
```bash
sudo dnf install -y \
    xcb-util-cursor xcb-util-icccm xcb-util-image xcb-util-keysyms \
    xcb-util-renderutil libxkbcommon-x11 \
    nss libXcomposite libXrandr libXdamage libdrm mesa-libgbm
```

**Without root access** (HPC clusters, shared systems) — install into the conda environment instead:
```bash
conda install -n beer -c conda-forge \
    xcb-util-cursor xcb-util-image xcb-util-keysyms xcb-util-renderutil \
    xcb-util-wm libxkbcommon xorg-libxrandr xorg-libxcomposite \
    xorg-libxdamage nss libdrm -y

mkdir -p $CONDA_PREFIX/etc/conda/activate.d
echo 'export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$CONDA_PREFIX/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH' \
    > $CONDA_PREFIX/etc/conda/activate.d/beer_xcb.sh
conda deactivate && conda activate beer
```

**macOS — AI features crash on first use:** BEER sets `KMP_DUPLICATE_LIB_OK=TRUE`
and `TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false` at startup to avoid a native segfault when the
ESMC backbone first loads (duplicate OpenMP runtime / tokenizers fork-parallelism).
If you still see a hard crash, run `beer` from a terminal — a Python/C stack trace
is now printed (via `faulthandler`); please attach it when reporting the issue.

---

## Model weights

The 24 prediction heads (~490 MB) are **not** bundled in the package — they
are hosted as assets on the [GitHub Release](https://github.com/chemgame/BEER/releases)
and downloaded automatically on first use into a per-user cache
(`~/.cache/beer/models`, or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\beer\models` on Windows). Each download
is verified against the sha256 in `beer/models/weights_manifest.json`. To use a
pre-downloaded or offline copy, point `BEER_MODELS_DIR` at a directory containing
the `.npz` files.

---

## Quick Start

```bash
conda activate beer
beer
```

1. Paste an amino-acid sequence (or drag-and-drop a `.fasta` file onto the window)
2. Click **Analyze** or press `Ctrl+Enter`
3. Browse the report sections in the left panel of the Analysis tab — click any section to display it
4. Click any section under **AI Predictions** to compute that BiLSTM head on demand
5. Go to the **Graphs** tab and click any graph name; right-click a graph to save it as PNG/SVG/PDF or export its data

Internet is only needed for external fetches (UniProt, AlphaFold, Pfam, ELM, DisProt, PhaSepDB, BLAST) and for the one-time download of the model weights. All analyses and AI predictions run on your computer.

**Privacy and network.** Two actions send your full sequence to an outside server: **BLAST** (NCBI) and **Predict Structure** (ESMFold2 via the Biohub Forge service). BEER asks before either one runs. Every other request sends only an accession or identifier. Under **Settings → Privacy and network**, *Offline mode* blocks every connection, including weight downloads, so switch it on only once the weights are cached. You can also turn off the upload confirmation there.

### CLI (headless) mode

BEER also runs without a display for batch use:

```bash
# Analyse a sequence, output JSON to stdout
beer analyze --sequence MADVFGKDMVNQ... --format json

# Analyse from a FASTA file, write HTML report
beer analyze --fasta my_protein.fasta --format html --output report.html

# Fetch from UniProt and export a TSV summary (skip ESMC for speed)
beer analyze --accession P04637 --format tsv --no-esmc --output p53.tsv

# Print version
beer version

# Show all commands and options
beer --help
beer analyze --help
```

Full flag list:

| Flag | Short | Description |
|------|-------|-------------|
| `--sequence` | `-s` | Protein sequence (single-letter code) |
| `--fasta` | `-f` | FASTA file path (first record used) |
| `--accession` | `-a` | UniProt or PDB accession to fetch |
| `--output` | `-o` | Output file (default: stdout) |
| `--format` | | `json` (default), `csv`, `tsv`, `html` |
| `--window` | `-w` | Sliding window size (default: 9) |
| `--hydro-scale` | | Hydrophobicity scale name |
| `--no-esmc` | | Skip BiLSTM predictions |
| `--sections` | | Report only specified sections |
| `--accent` | | Accent colour hex for HTML output |

---

## Input Methods

| Method | How |
|--------|-----|
| **Paste sequence** | Type or paste a bare amino-acid string or FASTA block and click **Analyze** |
| **Import FASTA** | Click **Import FASTA** → select a `.fa` / `.fasta` file; multi-sequence files load all chains into the Multichain tab |
| **Import PDB** | Click **Import PDB** → select a `.pdb` file; all chains available in the Chain dropdown |
| **Fetch UniProt** | Type a UniProt accession (e.g. `P04637`) → click **Fetch**; unlocks AlphaFold, Pfam, DisProt, PhaSepDB buttons and shows a protein summary |
| **Fetch PDB ID** | Type a 4-character RCSB code (e.g. `1UBQ`) → click **Fetch**; loads structure and all chains automatically |
| **Drag & Drop** | Drag a `.fasta` file directly onto the BEER window |
| **History** | A dropdown next to the toolbar lists the last 10 sequences analysed in the current session; selecting one re-runs the full analysis immediately. History is cleared when you close the app. |

---

## Analysis Tab

After running analysis, the left panel lists 14 classical analysis sections and a separate **AI Predictions** group (collapsed by default). Click any section name to display it; click a group header or the ▶ arrow to expand or collapse it. The report panel has two tabs — **Report** (all sections) and **Alanine Scan** (systematic single-site Ala mutation scan with ΔGRAVY, ΔMW, ΔCharge, and ΔDisorder fraction).

When you fetch a protein from UniProt or RCSB, a compact **protein info bar** appears above the report panel, showing the protein name, gene, organism, and a one-line functional description.

### Toolbar

| Button | Action |
|--------|--------|
| **Analyze** | Run fast (classical) analysis (`Ctrl+Enter`) |
| **AI Analysis** | Run full ESMC BiLSTM analysis (all 24 heads at once) |
| **Mutate…** | Point-mutation dialog |
| **Save / Load Session** | Save or restore a `.beer` JSON session file |
| **Figure Composer** | Assemble a custom multi-panel publication figure |
| **Fetch** | Download sequence from UniProt or RCSB PDB |
| **Fetch AlphaFold** | Download predicted structure from EBI AlphaFold |
| **Fetch Pfam / ELM** | Domain and linear motif annotations |
| **DisProt / PhaSepDB** | Disorder and phase-separation database annotations |
| **MobiDB** | Consensus disorder annotations from MobiDB (fraction disordered, predictor count, disordered regions) |
| **Variants** | Natural variants and mutagenesis data from UniProt |
| **IntAct** | Curated binary interactions from the IntAct molecular interaction database (EBI); shows partner, detection method, MI-score, and PubMed link |

Residues in the sequence viewer are colour-coded by type. Use the **Search** / **Highlight** box to find motifs or regex patterns. Below the viewer: **Copy Sequence** (whole or range) and **Clear All** (resets everything).

### Classical analysis sections

These 14 sections are always computed when you click **Analyze** (no ESMC required):

| Section | Contents |
|---------|----------|
| **Composition** | AA counts and frequencies, sortable by name / frequency / hydrophobicity |
| **Properties** | MW, pI, GRAVY, aromaticity, aliphatic index, extinction coefficient, instability index, estimated half-life |
| **Hydrophobicity** | Sliding-window hydrophobicity profile; scale selectable in Settings (Kyte-Doolittle, Eisenberg, Wimley-White, Hessa, Moon-Fleming, GES, Hopp-Woods, Fauchère-Pliska, Urry); y-axis label, units, and the ⓘ tooltip all update to reflect the chosen scale |
| **Charge** | FCR, NCPR, κ, Ω, net charge, charge asymmetry |
| **Aromatic & π** | Aromatic fraction, cation–π and π–π pair counts |
| **Repeat Motifs** | Shannon entropy, prion-like score, LC fraction, PLAAC score (Lancaster et al. 2014), PolyX stretches |
| **Sticker & Spacer** | Sticker count/spacing, **catGRANULE score** (Bolognesi et al. 2016 Cell Reports 14:2535): linear combination of catRAPID, disorder, and inverse hydrophobicity; score > 0 predicts condensate formation |
| **LARKS** | Low-complexity Aromatic-Rich Kinked Segments (Hughes et al. 2018) |
| **Linear Motifs** | Regex scan: NLS, NES, PxxP, 14-3-3, KFERQ, KDEL, SxIP, NxS/T, … |
| **β-Aggregation & Solubility** | ZYGGREGATOR hotspots (Tartaglia & Vendruscolo 2008); CamSol solubility (Sormanni et al. 2015) |
| **Amphipathic Helices** | Regions with μH ≥ 0.35 (Eisenberg 1984); hydrophobic moment profile for α-helix (δ=100°) and β-strand (δ=160°) |
| **Charge Decoration (SCD)** | Sequence charge decoration profile (Sawle & Ghosh 2015) |
| **Tandem Repeats** | Direct, tandem, and compositional repeats |
| **Proteolytic Map** | Predicted cleavage sites for 9 enzymes (Trypsin, Chymotrypsin, Lys-C, Asp-N, Glu-C, CNBr, Arg-C, Pepsin, Thermolysin); peptide masses in Da |

### AI Predictions sections

Computed on-demand when you click a section under **AI Predictions** in the sidebar (or click **AI Analysis** to run all 24 at once). Every profile tab has a **Show Uncertainty (MC-Dropout)** checkbox that adds ±1σ bands from 20 stochastic forward passes, for every head architecture (plain, CNN and positional BiLSTMs, the transmembrane BiLSTM-CRF and the secondary-structure head). Dropout is applied where the trained model applied it: on the CNN features, between LSTM layers and after the last LSTM layer.

**How each head is reported.** Every head section shows the head's decision threshold (the F1 maximum on its validation split), how many residues score above it, and a **protein-level call**: does this protein carry the feature at all?
- **Site heads** (active site, binding site, DNA/RNA/nucleotide binding, zinc finger, disulfide, and the five PTM heads), trained on single-residue annotations, list their predicted residues with scores.
- **Region heads** (disorder, coiled coil, intramembrane, low complexity, motif, propeptide, repeat, signal and transit peptides) list their predicted regions.
- A protein is called positive when it has a run of residues above the threshold at least as long as that head's minimum, chosen on the validation split. For site heads the minimum is one residue.
- The signal peptide and transit peptide runs must start within the first three residues.
- A transmembrane protein is reported when the Viterbi-decoded topology contains at least one transmembrane segment of 12 or more residues.
  - The minimum was chosen on the validation split: UniProt's annotations include β-barrel strands and 13–17-residue helices.
  - Very hydrophobic amphipathic helices in soluble proteins can occasionally decode as short segments.
- Heads that separate proteins with and without the feature only weakly (protein-level AUROC below 0.80 on the validation split: acetylation, ubiquitination and functional motifs) make no protein-level call and show their residue scores only.

| Head | Notes |
|------|-------|
| **Disorder** | Trained on experimental labels only: DisProt disordered regions, with residues observed in PDB structures as ordered; requires ESMC — there is no classical or metapredict substitute |
| **Signal Peptide** | AUROC 0.9997; classical Von Heijne D-score and AXA motif shown alongside; GPI anchor detection |
| **Transmembrane** | Trained on PDBTM membrane segments; BiLSTM-CRF with Viterbi topology decoding (outside → membrane → inside); transmembrane segments of ≥12 residues are reported; AUROC 0.9889, the predicted number of membrane segments matches the annotated number for 0.930 of test proteins |
| **Intramembrane** | Re-entrant membrane loops |
| **Coiled Coil** | Trained on UniProt coiled-coil regions, which UniProt assigns almost entirely by sequence analysis |
| **DNA Binding** | Trained on BioLiP structure-derived protein-DNA contacts |
| **RNA Binding** | Trained on BioLiP protein-RNA contacts and UniProt RNA-binding regions |
| **Active Site** | Trained on M-CSA mechanistically validated catalytic residues |
| **Binding Site** | Trained on BioLiP small-molecule binding residues |
| **Phosphorylation** | Trained on dbPTM experimental sites |
| **Ubiquitination** | Trained on dbPTM |
| **Methylation** | Trained on dbPTM |
| **Acetylation** | Trained on dbPTM |
| **Glycosylation** | Trained on UniProt glycosylation sites, most of which UniProt assigns by sequence analysis |
| **Lipidation** | |
| **Disulfide Bond** | |
| **Zinc Finger** | Trained on BioLiP Zn-coordinating residues |
| **Nucleotide Binding** | Trained on BioLiP (ATP/ADP/NAD/FAD/CoA/…) |
| **Low Complexity** | Trained on UniProt compositional-bias regions, which UniProt assigns by sequence analysis |
| **Functional Motif** | |
| **Propeptide** | |
| **Repeat Region** | |
| **Transit Peptide** | The transit-peptide and signal-peptide heads often both fire on the same N-terminus; treat a call by either as evidence of an N-terminal targeting sequence |
| **SS3: α-Helix** | Per-residue softmax probability that a residue is in an α-helix; output of the Q3 secondary structure head |
| **SS3: β-Strand** | Per-residue softmax probability of β-strand (sheet) assignment |
| **SS3: Coil/Loop** | Per-residue softmax probability of coil/loop assignment; the three SS3 profiles sum to 1.0 at every position |

---

## Graphs Tab

Navigate using the **category tree** on the left (all groups collapsed by default; click a group header or the ▶ arrow to expand it). The matplotlib toolbar (zoom, pan, home) appears above each figure. Click the **ⓘ** button (bottom-right of each graph) for a detailed description, equations, and references. **Right-click any graph** for three options: copy to clipboard, save figure (PNG/SVG/PDF), or **Export Graph Data…** — writes the underlying data (residue scores, domain lists, site tables, etc.) to a CSV or JSON file so you can re-plot or analyse it with external tools.

After fetching **UniProt annotation tracks** (via the **Fetch UniProt Tracks** button in the toolbar), helix and strand annotations are overlaid as coloured spans on the corresponding SS3 profile graphs. Click **✕ Clear Tracks** in the Graphs toolbar to remove all UniProt overlays without re-running the analysis.

Each graph panel's toolbar has **Save** (the file format — PNG / SVG / PDF — is chosen in the save dialog's file-type selector), **Data** (export the underlying values), **Copy**, **All (ZIP)**, and **Bundle…** buttons. Heatmap-type graphs (Distance Map, Residue Contact Network, Cation–π Map, MSA Covariance, Single-Residue Perturbation Map, Variant Effect Map, AlphaMissense, Helical Wheel) also have a **Colormap dropdown** to switch the colour scheme per graph without touching Settings.

Individual graphs export per-section, or use the toolbar buttons: **Export All as ZIP** (all generated graphs as PNG) and **Publication Bundle…** — a one-click ZIP containing every generated figure as **vector** (SVG or PDF), each graph's underlying data, a combined wide per-residue CSV (`all_residue_tracks.csv`), the full report (`report.html`), and a `PROVENANCE.txt` recording the BEER version, date, and analysis parameters (pH, window, hydrophobicity scale, pKa set, ESMC model).

| Category | Graphs |
|----------|--------|
| **Composition** | Amino Acid Composition (Bar) |
| **AI Predictions** | Disorder Profile, Signal Peptide Profile, Transmembrane Profile, Intramembrane Profile, Coiled-Coil Profile, DNA-Binding Profile, RNA Binding Profile, Active Site Profile, Binding Site Profile, Phosphorylation Profile, Low-Complexity Profile, Zinc Finger Profile, Glycosylation Profile, Ubiquitination Profile, Methylation Profile, Acetylation Profile, Lipidation Profile, Disulfide Bond Profile, Functional Motif Profile, Propeptide Profile, Repeat Region Profile, Nucleotide-Binding Profile, Transit Peptide Profile, Secondary Structure: Helix Profile, Secondary Structure: Strand Profile, Secondary Structure: Coil Profile |
| **Other Sequence Profiles** | Hydrophobicity Profile, Local Charge Profile, SCD Profile, SHD Profile |
| **Charge & π-Interactions** | Isoelectric Focus, Charge Decoration, Cation–π Map |
| **Membrane & Amphipathicity** | TM Topology, Hydrophobic Moment, Helical Wheel |
| **Aggregation & Solubility** | β-Aggregation Profile, Solubility Profile |
| **Phase Separation & IDP** | Uversky Phase Plot, Single-Residue Perturbation Map, Sticker Map, PLAAC Profile |
| **Sequence Maps & Annotation** | Linear Sequence Map, Annotation Track, Domain Architecture, Cleavage Map |
| **AlphaFold & Structure**† | pLDDT / B-Factor Profile, SASA Profile, Distance Map, Residue Contact Network, Ramachandran Plot (MolProbity Top8000 per-class favored/allowed contours with per-residue outlier detection) |
| **Variant Effects**† | Variant Effect Map, AlphaMissense |
| **Evolutionary & Comparative** | MSA Conservation, MSA Covariance, Truncation Series, Complex Mass |

†Requires a loaded structure (AlphaFold fetch or PDB import) or UniProt fetch for variant data.

> **Reading the Variant Effect Map:** the colour scale is an ESMC **log-likelihood ratio (LLR)** — an evolutionary/language-model fitness score in log-probability units (nats), *not* a thermodynamic stability change (ΔΔG, kcal/mol). A favourable LLR means the substitution is sequence-plausible under the model, not that it stabilises the fold.

**pLDDT / B-Factor Profile**: when the structure was loaded from the AlphaFold EBI database the graph is titled "pLDDT Profile" with confidence-zone colouring (Very High ≥ 90, Confident 70–90, Low 50–70, Very Low < 50). When loaded from RCSB PDB or a local file the graph switches to "B-Factor Profile" with crystallographic B-factor zones (< 20 / 20–40 / 40–60 / > 60 Å²).

**Domain Architecture**: shows Pfam domains (UniProt fetch required), BEER AI disorder regions, and disordered linker spans. Transmembrane segments are not drawn here; they are listed in **AI Predictions → Transmembrane**, and the per-residue membrane probability is in the **Transmembrane Profile** graph.

---

## Structure Tab

Interactive 3D viewer powered by [Mol*](https://molstar.org) (bundled locally — fully offline, no CDN), embedded via Qt WebEngine. The tab has a **View** control panel, an **Interact** panel, and a **3D canvas**. The default background is white.

**View tab controls**

| Control | Options |
|---------|---------|
| **Representation** | Cartoon (default), Stick, Sphere, Line, Cross, Trace, Surface |
| **Color mode** | pLDDT/B-factor, Residue type, Chain, Charge, Hydrophobicity, Mass, Secondary Structure, Residue Number, Solvent Accessibility, AI Features, Aggregation |
| **Color scheme** | Mode-dependent: Red-White-Blue, Rainbow, Shapely, Cyan-White-Orange, JMol, PyMOL, Plasma, etc. |
| **Color bar** | Toggleable gradient/categorical legend overlay (bottom-right) |
| **H-bonds** | Toggle backbone N–O hydrogen bonds (< 3.5 Å); choose cylinder colour and radius |
| **Contacts (8 Å)** | Toggle Cα–Cα contact lines; choose line colour and opacity |
| **Background** | White (default), Black, Grey presets or custom color picker |
| **Spin** | Continuous auto-rotation on X / Y / Z axis |
| **Reset View** | Restores default representation (Cartoon), colour mode (pLDDT), clears selections, and resets camera |
| **Snapshot PNG** | Saves current view as PNG |
| **Chains** | Toggle visibility of individual chains |

**Interact tab** — residue selection (by number, range, name, or chain), distance / angle / dihedral measurements between clicked atoms.

**AlphaFold + ESMFold2 overlay** — when both an AlphaFold and an ESMFold2 structure are loaded, the viewer enters overlay mode with AlphaFold fixed to blue and ESMFold2 to orange, and the colour controls are locked so the two models stay visually distinct. Un-checking either model in the **Overlay** panel returns full colour control to the remaining structure — pick any colour mode/scheme and it applies immediately. Re-checking both models restores the locked blue/orange colouring.

**Export Structure / Sequence** saves in PDB, mmCIF, GRO, XYZ, or FASTA format. It also exports interoperability formats: a **GFF3** feature track of predicted regions, **PyMOL (.pml)** / **ChimeraX (.cxc)** scripts that reproduce a per-residue colouring (pick which AI track), and a **structure coloured by track (.pdb)** with the chosen track written into the B-factor column so any viewer can colour by it.

---

## Other Tabs

| Tab | What it does |
|-----|-------------|
| **Fix PDB** | Completes an experimental structure with missing residues: fetch by PDB ID, then fill the gaps with a predicted model. On fetch the structure is reduced to protein atoms — water, ions, and ligands are stripped (modified residues such as selenomethionine are kept) so heteroatoms cannot disturb the gap alignment. **Fix PDB** uses the matching **AlphaFold** model (enter the UniProt accession); **Fix with ESMFold2** folds the chain's sequence via the BioHub Forge API and fills the gaps with it — no accession needed, but requires a **BioHub API key**. The folded sequence is reconstructed from the experimental chain's resolved residue range with placeholder residues at the unresolved positions, so the prediction contains a residue for every gap (gap backbones are transplanted; their identities are placeholders — use the AlphaFold path when exact gap residue identities matter). Use the ESMFold2 path when no AlphaFold model is available. Experimental atoms keep occupancy 1.00, gap-fill atoms 0.00, and REMARK records record the gap-fill source. |
| **BLAST** | Submits current sequence to NCBI blastp (1–3 min); click **Load** on any hit to re-run analysis on that sequence |
| **Multichain** | Auto-populated from multi-FASTA or multi-chain PDB; shows MW, charge, composition per chain; double-click a row to load it |
| **Compare** | Side-by-side property table and profile overlays for two sequences |
| **Truncation** | Computes properties across progressive N/C truncations and generates the Truncation Series graph |
| **MSA** | Paste a multi-FASTA alignment → per-column conservation graph + residue covariance heatmap (MI with APC; requires ≥4 sequences, ≤500 columns). The preview pane shows **Open …graph** links that jump straight to the rendered graph — no separate Analysis run needed. **Export PSSM (CSV)** writes a position-specific scoring matrix (log₂ odds vs. Swiss-Prot background) with per-column consensus, coverage, and conservation |
| **Complex** | Paste chains + stoichiometry (e.g. `A2B1`) → total MW, extinction coefficients, bar chart |
| **Help** | Built-in reference; **Copy Citation (BibTeX)** and **Generate Methods Paragraph** buttons |

## ESMC Neural Predictions

The AI Predictions heads use EvolutionaryScale's ESMC 600M protein language model. The ESMC backbone (~2.3 GB) downloads automatically on the first AI Predictions call and caches in the local Hugging Face / ESM cache — this only happens once.

**On-demand computation**: each head is computed only when you click it; the embedding is cached after the first head, so all subsequent heads are fast. Running **AI Analysis** computes all available heads at once.

**Sequence length**: all 24 heads were trained on sequences truncated to **1024 residues** — no head saw a residue beyond position 1024 during training. There is **no hard cap at inference**: longer proteins are embedded and scored end-to-end and always produce a full-length profile, but per-residue predictions **beyond residue 1024 are extrapolation** and should be interpreted with caution. BEER shows a one-time notice when you run an AI head on a sequence longer than 1024 residues. Classical (non-AI) analyses have no length limit.

If ESMC is not installed, the AI Predictions heads — including the disorder profile — are simply unavailable; BEER does not substitute a classical or third-party predictor for any feature that has an AI head. The composition-based disorder-promoting fraction in the Properties section, and all other classical analysis, still run fully offline without ESMC.

---

## Metrics Reference

### Sequence properties

| Metric | Definition |
|--------|-----------|
| MW | Sum of residue masses + water (Da) |
| pI | pH where net charge = 0 (Henderson-Hasselbalch) |
| GRAVY | Mean Kyte-Doolittle hydropathicity |
| Aromaticity | (F + W + Y) / length |
| Extinction coefficient | W×5500 + Y×1490 + (C–C)×125 at 280 nm |
| Instability index | Guruprasad (1990) dipeptide-weight sum; < 40 predicts a stable protein in vitro |
| Estimated half-life | In-vivo half-life from the N-terminal residue (N-end rule, mammalian; Bachmair 1986) |
| FCR | (K + R + D + E) / length |
| NCPR | (positive − negative) / length |
| κ (kappa) | Charge patterning: 0 = well-mixed, 1 = fully segregated (Das & Pappu 2013) |
| Ω (omega) | Sticker patterning, same scale as κ |

### IDP / Phase separation

| Metric | Definition |
|--------|-----------|
| Aliphatic index | 100 × (A + 2.9V + 3.9(I+L)) / length; higher values indicate greater thermostability (Ikai 1980) |
| LARKS | 7-residue windows: ≥1 aromatic, ≥50% LC residues, entropy < 1.8 bit (Hughes et al. 2018) |
| SCD | Pairwise charge product weighted by sequence separation (Sawle & Ghosh 2015) |
| PLAAC score | Per-residue log-odds of yeast prion-like FG vs SwissProt background, window = 41 (Lancaster et al. 2014) |
| PolyX stretch | Run of ≥4 identical consecutive residues |
| Prion-like score | Fraction of N, Q, S, G, Y residues |
| ZYGGREGATOR | Per-residue β-aggregation propensity; hotspots flagged where score ≥ 1.0 over ≥ 4 consecutive residues (Tartaglia & Vendruscolo 2008) |
| CamSol | Intrinsic solubility scale (Sormanni et al. 2015) |

---

## Recent changes

- **Calibrated probabilities:** the AI heads now report probabilities on a calibrated scale. The scale is fitted to each head's validation data, which contain far more proteins with the feature than a typical proteome. Read a score as a ranking and compare it with the head's threshold. It is not the chance that a residue in your protein carries the feature. Each head's decision threshold moves with its scores, so every prediction BEER makes is unchanged, and the thresholds shown in the interface are lower than before. Two heads are unaffected: transmembrane, which decodes with a CRF, and secondary structure, which picks the highest of three classes.
- **Offline mode and upload confirmation:** BEER now asks before sending a sequence to an outside server, and an offline switch blocks every connection.
- **Measured error rates beside each call:** every protein-level call now states how often its rule called proteins with and without the feature on held-out test proteins.
- **Quieter start-up:** ESM C's notices about optional CUDA kernels (Transformer Engine, xformers, flash-attn) no longer appear on every launch. They describe differences far below the precision of any prediction, and they cannot be acted on without a graphics card. Set `BEER_LOG_ESM=1` to see them.
- **Graph rendering fix:** a graph could fail to appear, with a toolbar error in the log, after several graphs had been drawn. Old graph widgets are now handed to Qt for deletion instead of being left to Python, and a graph still opens even if its toolbar cannot be built.
- **Protein-level calls for more heads:** whether a head makes a protein-level call is now decided on its validation data. Phosphorylation, methylation and lipidation now make calls. Their measured error rates, shown beside each call, are weaker than for the other heads. The repeat head now also reports calibrated probabilities.
- **New disorder head:** the disorder predictor is retrained on experimental labels only (DisProt disordered regions, with residues seen in PDB structures as ordered). It is more accurate on independent disorder benchmarks. A protein is now reported as having a disordered region when at least 10 consecutive residues are above the threshold.
- **Signal and transit peptides:** the report now notes that the signal-peptide and transit-peptide heads often both fire on the same N-terminus.
- **Signal peptide section follows the protein-level rule:** the Signal Peptide section of the report now uses the same rule as the protein-level call and gives the predicted cleavage position. Earlier it averaged the probability over the first 70 residues, which could label a short signal peptide as unlikely.
- **Training sources stated correctly:** the Help table and each AI section now name the data each head was actually trained on, including where UniProt annotations are mostly assigned by sequence analysis.
- **Hydropathy decoration corrected:** the SHD profile now follows the published definition of Zheng et al. (2020) and its hydropathy scale. Earlier SHD values are not comparable.
- **Transmembrane report fix:** the Report tab could state "no transmembrane segment" for a membrane protein whose profile clearly showed membrane helices. The segments are now carried through reliably, including after applying settings, so the report and the profile agree.
- **Worker shutdown fix:** cancelling an analysis or starting a new one while an AI prediction was still running could raise a `TypeError` while the prediction was being retired, and the results it was carrying were lost. Predictions are now retired cleanly whatever they were computing.
- **Improved binding and secondary-structure heads:** the five heads trained on structure-derived contacts (DNA, RNA, nucleotide, ligand and zinc binding) now learn from full-length proteins, and the secondary-structure head learns from DSSP assignments. Accuracy rose for all six, and binding predictions no longer depend on whether a domain is scored alone or inside its whole protein.
- **Protein-level rules per head:** the minimum run of residues needed to call a protein positive is now set for each head from its validation split.
- **Model attribution:** a `NOTICE` file credits the ESM C 600M model (MIT licence, Chan Zuckerberg Biohub) that BEER downloads for its AI predictions. The source code remains GPL v3.
- **v3.1 prediction heads:** all 24 heads are trained with proteins that lack each feature as negatives. Each head's decision threshold is chosen on a validation split, and the AUROCs shown throughout BEER are measured on a held-out test split. Cached v3.0 weights are replaced automatically on first use.
- **v3.2 weights:** head weights now download from the v3.2.0 release. A cached disorder head from v3.1 is replaced automatically on first use.
- **Protein-level calls:** every AI section states whether the protein carries the feature, using that head's calibrated threshold. Site heads list their predicted residues and region heads their predicted regions.
- **Transmembrane segments:** membrane segments of at least 12 residues from the Viterbi topology are reported as transmembrane segments.
- **Uncertainty for every head:** the MC-dropout uncertainty band is available for all 24 heads.
- **Command line:** `beer --help` and `beer -h` print usage. Qt options such as `-platform` launch the GUI.
- **Performance:** 19 of 24 AI prediction heads are now deferred — `analyze_sequence` completes in seconds; each head runs on demand via `AISectionWorker` when you open its section or click "AI Analysis".
- **Robustness:** Truncation series analysis now runs in a background thread with a cancellable progress dialog, keeping the UI responsive for long sequences.
- **Variant Effect Map:** ESMC inference for the variant heatmap runs off the main thread; a placeholder is shown immediately while the background worker computes.
- **Thread safety:** `ESMCEmbedder` is now fully thread-safe (RLock-guarded LRU cache; inference runs outside the lock).
- **Input validation:** UniProt accession and PDB ID inputs are validated before any network request, with informative error messages for malformed IDs.
- **Packaging:** `molstar.js`, `molstar.css`, and `struct_viewer.html` are correctly listed in `pyproject.toml` and `MANIFEST.in`.
- **Session loading:** `_apply_session_defaults` now always runs on load, preventing `KeyError` for sessions written by older BEER versions.
- **CLI `beer analyze`:** Fixed `ImportError: cannot import name 'analyze_sequence'` — module-level alias added.
- **Sidebar grouping:** the left navigation is now grouped into four labelled clusters (Analysis · Structure · Compare/Evolve · System) with Settings/Help at the bottom; keyboard shortcuts are unchanged.
- **Structure overlay colours:** Hiding one model in an AlphaFold + ESMFold2 overlay now restores full colour control to the visible structure (colour changes apply immediately); the fixed blue/orange lock returns only when both models are shown again.
- **Multi-chain PDB handling:** Fetching or importing a multi-chain PDB/mmCIF now keeps the full assembly in the 3D viewer when you switch chains — selecting a chain updates the per-chain profiles (pLDDT, distance map, Ramachandran, SASA) without collapsing the structure or removing the chain-visibility controls. Per-chain analysis for the Multichain table and chain selector now runs classical-only, so all chains populate immediately instead of waiting on a full ESMC pass per chain (AI heads are still computed on demand per chain).
- **Structure prediction:** *Predict Structure* and *Fix with ESMFold2* fold with the ESMFold2 model (`esmfold2-2026-05`) on the Biohub Forge service.
- **Long-sequence AI notice:** the 24 AI heads were trained on sequences truncated to 1024 residues. Running an AI head on a longer protein now shows a one-time notice that predictions beyond residue 1024 are extrapolation; the sequence is still scored end-to-end and classical analyses are unaffected.

- **Source code and prediction-head weights:** GNU General Public License v3. See `LICENSE`.
- **ESM C 600M:** MIT licence (Chan Zuckerberg Biohub), downloaded on first use from [biohub/ESMC-600M](https://huggingface.co/biohub/ESMC-600M). See `NOTICE`.

## 是什么
IDP-o 是一个基于片段的固有无序蛋白（IDP）构象系综生成器。它将蛋白质序列切分为 6 个残基长的片段（片段间重叠 2 个残基），在结构数据库中搜索匹配片段，然后拼接这些片段以生成一组构象系综，并推断氢原子，使生成的构象可直接用于下游任务。

## 亮点
- **片段拼接策略**：通过将长序列分解为短片段并在结构数据库中搜索，避免了从头预测的复杂性，能够高效生成多样化的构象系综。
- **集成氢原子推断**：生成的构象包含氢原子，可直接用于分子动力学模拟或对接等下游任务，省去预处理步骤。
- **容器化部署**：提供 Docker 镜像，简化环境配置，支持 GPU 加速，便于大规模运行。
- **数据库自动化**：提供脚本自动下载 foldcomp 数据库并生成所需格式的 FASTA 文件，降低使用门槛。

## 为何对本课题有用
IDP-o 直接针对 IDR/IDP 的构象系综生成，是 IDP 研究中的核心工具。它通过片段拼接方法，能够快速生成符合物理化学性质的构象集合，可用于：
- 作为 IDP 构象系综的基准或输入，用于训练或验证无序蛋白语言模型。
- 为分子互作（如 LLPS）建模提供初始构象，支持后续的粗粒化或全原子模拟。
- 其片段搜索和拼接逻辑可迁移到其他无序区域建模任务，例如预测 IDR 的构象偏好。

## 怎么用
- **主入口**：`scripts/build_ensemble.py`，通过 Docker 运行，命令示例见 README。
- **安装与依赖**：使用 Docker 构建镜像（`docker build --platform=linux/amd64 . -t idp-o`），依赖包括 `foldcomp`、`tables`、`cupy-cuda12x`、`hirola`、`pynmrstar`、`joblib` 以及 `nerfax`（见 Dockerfile）。
- **输入数据**：蛋白质序列（FASTA 格式）和 foldcomp 数据库（`afdb_uniprot_v4`），需先运行 `scripts/prepare_foldcomp_fasta.py` 生成特殊格式的 FASTA 文件。
- **输出数据**：HDF5 文件（如 `ensemble.h5`），包含构象系综。
- **GPU 需求**：需要 GPU 加速（Docker 命令中 `--gpus 1`）。
- **调试示例**：README 提供了生成单个序列系综的示例命令，可断点调试；`generate_dataset.py` 用于批量生成数据集。

## 核心 idea
IDP-o 的核心方法学是“片段拼接”：将长 IDP 序列分解为短片段，在结构数据库中搜索匹配片段，然后拼接这些片段以生成构象系综。这种方法利用了数据库中已有的结构信息，避免了从头预测的昂贵计算，同时通过片段重叠和拼接策略保持了构象的多样性，从而高效生成物理上合理的 IDP 构象集合。

## 可搬移点
- **片段搜索与拼接逻辑**：`scripts/fasta_search_in_foldcomp_database.py` 和 `scripts/join_fragments.py` 中的核心算法可被解耦，用于自定义的 IDP 构象生成流程，例如替换为其他结构数据库或调整片段长度。
- **氢原子推断模块**：`nerfax` 库（依赖中）可能包含氢原子推断功能，可独立使用。
- **数据库准备脚本**：`scripts/prepare_foldcomp_fasta.py` 可复用，用于处理其他 foldcomp 数据库。
- **License**：Apache 2.0，允许自由使用和修改，但需保留版权声明。

# IDP-o: Fragment-based Intrinsically Disordered Protein Ensemble Generator

[![bioRxiv](https://img.shields.io/badge/bioRxiv-2025.10.18.680935-b31b1b.svg)](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.10.18.680935v2)
[![DOI](https://zenodo.org/badge/DOI/10.5281/zenodo.17306061.svg)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17306061)
[![Source Code](https://img.shields.io/badge/-PeptoneBench-000000?style=flat&logo=github&logoColor=ffffff&labelColor=gray)](https://github.com/PeptoneLtd/PeptoneBench)
[![Source Code](https://img.shields.io/badge/-PepTron-000000?style=flat&logo=github&logoColor=ffffff&labelColor=gray)](https://github.com/PeptoneLtd/PepTron)

IDP-o cuts a protein sequence into 6 long fragments, with overlap of 2 residues between fragments. Searches in a structure database, then stitches those fragments together to make an ensemble of configurations. Configurations have hydrogens inferred so one can use it directly in downstream tasks.

![IDP-o workflow](assets/idp-o.png)


## Build docker image
```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/PeptoneLtd/IDP-o
cd IDP-o

# Build Docker container
docker build --platform=linux/amd64 . -t idp-o
```

## Download the foldcomp database and generate the foldcomp fasta file
IDP-o needs a specially formatted fasta file to work properly. The format is:

```
> {offet in bytes in the foldcomp db}
{sequence}
> {offet in bytes in the foldcomp db}
{sequence}
...
```
Such file is not directly distributed by foldcomp, but can be easily generated. We provide a convenience script to automate the download of the foldcomp database and the creation of this special fasta file:

```bash
docker run -v $(pwd):/data --entrypoint python idp-o /IDP-o/scripts/prepare_foldcomp_fasta.py --workdir /data
```

This will download the `afdb_uniprot_v4` foldcomp database in the current directory (~1.1 T), and generate the `afdb_uniprot_v4.fasta` file needed to run IDP-o


## Generating ensembles
```bash
docker run -v $(pwd):/data --gpus 1 \
  idp-o \
    --sequence DLIVERANDSANDRDANDCARLDANDMICHELEANDLDHIEANDFADIDANDSTEFANDANDISTVANANDALDERTANDDLIVERAGAINPLASDTHERS \
    --outpath /data/example/ensemble.h5 \
    --scratch_folder /data/example/ \
    --foldcomp_fasta /data/afdb_uniprot_v4.fasta \
    --foldcomp_db /data/afdb_uniprot_v4 \
    --n_max_structures_per_fragment 100
```
Note: the final fragment can be smaller than 6 residues, depending on sequence length.

The script `generate_dataset.py` provides a simple wrapper for generating a full dataset, like [IDRome-o](https://zenodo.org/records/17306061).

## Citation
```bibtex

  title     = {Advancing Protein Ensemble Predictions Across the Order-Disorder Continuum},
```

## 是什么
OpenPhase 是一个开源平台和数据集，旨在加速生物分子液-液相分离（LLPS）的知识发现。它是首个条件感知（condition-aware）的系统级探索平台，用于研究环境因素（如盐浓度、温度、pH 等）如何影响生物分子的相行为。仓库提供了按系统组织的实验记录数据集、标准化的基准任务（结果预测、条件推断、系统设计）以及相应的扩散模型实现（离散扩散和潜在扩散）。

## 亮点
- **条件感知建模**：明确将环境条件（盐浓度、温度、pH 等）纳入建模，超越仅基于序列的预测。
- **大规模、多系统数据集**：整合了来自 LLPSDB v2、LLPSense、RNAPSEC、PhaSepDB 3 等来源的 11,439 条单蛋白实验记录，以及 35,107 个负样本/未标记蛋白，按系统（蛋白、蛋白+RNA、蛋白+DNA、蛋白饱和浓度）组织。
- **标准化基准**：为三个规范任务（结果预测、条件推断、系统设计）提供了标准化的训练/测试划分、基线模型和评估指标。
- **交互式探索网站**：提供浏览器端运行的交互式数据探索界面，支持系统图点击导航和明暗主题切换。
- **模块化代码结构**：包含独立的扩散模型实现（Discrete/ 和 ldm/），以及原始数据源的归档加载器（zhanglab/）。

## 为何对本课题有用
OpenPhase 直接针对 IDR/IDP 与 LLPS 的交叉领域，提供了：
- **条件感知的相分离数据**：包含环境条件（盐、温度、pH）的标注，这对于研究 IDR 的相行为至关重要，因为 IDR 的相分离高度依赖环境。
- **标准化的基准任务**：为结果预测、条件推断和系统设计提供了明确的评估协议，可直接用于比较和开发新的预测模型。
- **扩散模型实现**：提供了离散和潜在扩散模型的代码，可用于生成具有目标相行为的多肽序列，这对于 IDP 设计具有直接价值。
- **负样本和未标记数据**：提供了 35,107 个负样本/未标记蛋白，有助于训练更稳健的分类器，避免正样本偏差。

## 怎么用
- **主入口**：`openphase_systems.py` 提供加载数据集的接口；`task1.py`、`task2.py`、`task3.py` 分别对应三个规范任务。
- **安装**：`git clone https://github.com/nicetone9/OpenPhase.git`，依赖见 `requirements.txt` 或 `setup.py`（README 未列出具体依赖文件内容）。
- **数据加载示例**：
  ```python
  from openphase_systems import list_systems, load_system
  list_systems()
  rna = load_system("protein_RNA")
  ```
- **数据格式**：数据以 pandas DataFrame 形式加载，包含序列、条件、来源等信息；原始数据源有各自的加载器（`zhanglab/db1.py` 等）。
- **GPU 需求**：扩散模型训练和推理可能需要 GPU 加速，但 README 未明确说明。
- **调试入口**：`records_space/colab/` 下有多个 Colab 脚本（如 `drv_export.py`、`rs03_run.py`），可用于复现数据构建和探索流程；`test_rslib.py` 提供单元测试。

## 核心 idea
OpenPhase 的核心方法学洞察是：将环境条件作为一等公民纳入相分离预测和生成模型，通过系统级的数据组织和标准化的任务定义，使得模型能够学习条件与相行为之间的映射关系，从而实现条件推断和条件感知的序列设计。

## 可搬移点
- **数据加载与整合逻辑**：`openphase_systems.py` 和 `zhanglab/` 下的加载器展示了如何整合多个来源的数据并去重，可迁移到其他 IDP/LLPS 数据集的构建。
- **条件感知的扩散模型**：`Discrete/` 和 `ldm/` 中的扩散模型实现（如 `Discrete/protein_diffusion_model.py`、`ldm/ldm_minimal/diffusion/unet_denoising_esmc.py`）可被解耦并用于自定义的序列生成任务，特别是条件生成。
- **基准任务定义**：`task1.py`、`task2.py`、`task3.py` 中的任务划分和评估协议可复用于其他 LLPS 预测模型的基准测试。
- **负样本构建方法**：`records_space/` 中的负样本和未标记数据构建流程（如 PPMC 与 Swiss-Prot 参考样本的比较）可借鉴用于构建更平衡的训练集。
- **License**：README 未明确说明许可证，需确认。

Open the OpenPhase site  ·  Records and protein universe (P)  ·  Negatives and unlabelled (N + U)

# OpenPhase OpenPhase: Condition-Aware Exploration of Biomolecular Phase Separation OpenPhase is an open-source platform and dataset designed to accelerate knowledge discovery in Liquid-Liquid Phase Separation (LLPS). It is the first condition-aware platform for system-level exploration of how environmental factors influence biomolecular phase behavior. ## 🌐 Interactive site **[nicetone9.github.io/OpenPhase](https://nicetone9.github.io/OpenPhase/)** is the home page of the OpenPhase data resources. Click a part of the system figures to open the explorer on that system; every page has a light / dark switch and runs entirely in the browser. | System | What it holds | Page | |---|---|---| | **P** | 11,439 single-protein experiment records in one map, plus 6,338 proteins that the tools list as positives but that have no record (hollow rings) | [records_space/](https://nicetone9.github.io/OpenPhase/records_space/) | | **N + U** | 35,107 proteins: the training negatives of ten tools and PPMC against a Swiss-Prot reference sample. No positives, no conditions | [records_space/negatives/](https://nicetone9.github.io/OpenPhase/records_space/negatives/) | Multi-protein systems (protein(2), protein(3), complexes) are shown on the home page but are not in the explorer yet. Details, data notes and licences: [`records_space/README.md`](records_space/README.md). ## 🚀 Key Features ### Condition-Aware Modeling Moves beyond simple sequence prediction to incorporate extrinsic environmental factors (salt concentration, temperature, pH, etc.) that critically influence phase separation behavior. ### Comprehensive Datasets, organised by system The records are organised by **system** (the set of components of an experiment, without concentrations); see [`data/`](data/README.md). | System | Records | Folder | |---|---:|---| | protein only | 7,490 | `data/protein/` | | protein + RNA | 2,511 | `data/protein_RNA/` | | protein + DNA | 662 | `data/protein_DNA/` | | protein, saturation concentration | 776 | `data/protein_csat/` | Records come from LLPSDB v2, LLPSense, RNAPSEC, a PhaSepDB 3 pilot extraction, Bremer 2022 and Ausserwöger 2025, merged and de-duplicated. A nucleic acid is one of the conditions of a record. The three original sources keep their loaders, archived in [`zhanglab/`](zhanglab/README.md): - **db1** (`zhanglab/db1.py`): processed LLPSDBv2 data containing proteins, RNA, and DNA sequences with phase separation annotations - **db2** (`zhanglab/db2.py`): manually collected records from laboratory notebooks covering both in vitro and in vivo experiments (not in the tables of `data/`) - **db3** (`zhanglab/db3.py`): preprocessed RNAPSEC data focused on protein-RNA interaction systems and their phase behavior ### Standardized Benchmarking Formalized tasks and evaluation protocols for: - Outcome prediction - Condition inference - Protein design - Reproducible research in LLPS ## 🛠️ Canonical Tasks ### 1. Phase Outcome Prediction Predicting whether a system undergoes LLPS (y ∈ {0, 1}) given: - Components (x): protein/RNA sequences - Conditions (c): environmental factors (pH, salt, temperature, etc.) ### 2. Condition Inference Inferring the potential experimental conditions (c) that lead to a specific phase separation outcome, enabling rational experimental design. ### 3. Phase System Design Generating potential protein sequences (x) that exhibit desired phase behaviors under target conditions using generative models. ## 📂 Repository Structure ``` OpenPhase/ ├── data/ # records by system (protein, protein_RNA, protein_DNA, protein_csat) ├── openphase_systems.py # load the records by system ├── zhanglab/ # archived loaders of the three original sources │ ├── db1.py # LLPSDBv2 dataset interface │ ├── db2.py # Laboratory notebook dataset │ └── db3.py # RNAPSEC dataset interface ├── Discrete/ # Discrete diffusion model ├── ldm/ # Latent diffusion model components ├── MTDP/ # MTDP embedder ├── records_space/ # records space and protein universe explorer ├── meta_config.py # Configuration utilities ├── meta_embed.py # Embedding generation └── params_all.yaml # Global hyperparameters ``` ## 🔧 Installation ```bash git clone https://github.com/nicetone9/OpenPhase.git cd OpenPhase # Install dependencies (see requirements.txt or setup.py) ``` ## 📊 Getting Started Load the records by system: ```python from openphase_systems import list_systems, load_system list_systems() # records, sequences, papers and sources of each system rna = load_system("protein_RNA") # a pandas data frame; load_system("protein_RNA", source="RNAPSEC") ``` Build the embedded datasets of the three original sources: ```python from zhanglab.db1 import DB1Dataset from zhanglab.db2 import DB2Dataset from zhanglab.db3 import DB3Dataset db1 = DB1Dataset() db2 = DB2Dataset() db3 = DB3Dataset() ``` ## 📚 Tasks & Benchmarks Each canonical task includes: - Standardized train/test splits - Baseline models - Evaluation metrics - Documentation in `task1.py`, `task2.py`, `task3.py` ## 🤝 Contributing Contributions are welcome! Please refer to contribution guidelines and open issues for ongoing research directions. ## 📖 Citation If you use ConditionPhase in your research, please cite the associated publication. ## 📧 Contact For questions, suggestions, or collaborations, visit the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/nicetone9/ConditionPhase) and contact [email](peiran@cmu.edu).

## 是什么

mdSAM 是一个用于发现膜蛋白固有无序区中自组装基序（membrane-disordered Self-Assembly Motifs）的分析与复现仓库。它提供了一套从人类蛋白质组中识别、表征并验证 mdSAM 的完整计算流程，包括随机森林分类器训练、无序区判定、序列空间分析、体外聚集实验数据处理、细胞成像统计以及进化保守性分析。该仓库以 23 个 Jupyter notebook 的形式组织，对应论文中的各个图表。

## 亮点

- **端到端可复现**：每个论文图面板都通过 `FIGURE_MAP.csv` 精确映射到具体的 notebook 和 cell，便于逐图复现。
- **模块化分析流程**：从数据准备、分类器训练、序列特征分析到实验数据统计，每个环节独立成 notebook，便于局部修改和复用。
- **多维度验证**：整合了生物物理（ThT 荧光）、细胞成像（TIRF、dSTORM）、信号转导（cAMP）和转录组（RNA-seq）等多层次数据，形成完整的验证链条。
- **利用 AlphaFold 结构信息**：通过 pLDDT 分数定义无序区，将结构预测与序列基序发现结合。
- **丰富的第三方数据整合**：使用 WALTZ-DB 2.0、UniProt、hyperLOPIT、BioGRID 等公开资源，增强分析的广度和可信度。

## 为何对本课题有用

该仓库直接针对 IDR/IDP 与分子互作的核心问题：它提出并验证了膜蛋白无序区中的短肽基序（mdSAM）能够通过 β-strand 介导的类淀粉样相互作用驱动自组装和膜表面聚集。对于 IDR/IDP × LLPS × AI/模拟 课题，其价值体现在：

- **无序区功能基序的识别方法**：展示了如何利用随机森林分类器（基于 WALTZ-DB 2.0 训练）和 AlphaFold pLDDT 阈值来系统性地发现无序区中的自组装基序，该方法可迁移到其他 IDR 功能基序的预测。
- **序列-功能关联分析**：通过序列空间嵌入、GMM 聚类和关键字富集，揭示了 mdSAM 的序列多样性和功能相关性，为理解 IDR 介导的互作特异性提供了范例。
- **实验验证与计算预测的闭环**：从预测到体外聚集实验（ThT）、细胞成像（TIRF/dSTORM）和信号功能验证，展示了如何将计算发现与实验验证紧密结合，这对 IDR 互作研究具有方法论参考价值。
- **进化保守性分析**：利用序列比对和蛋白质语言模型嵌入（ESM）评估 mdSAM 的保守性，为 IDR 功能位点的进化约束提供了新视角。

## 怎么用

- **主入口**：仓库以 Jupyter notebook 为主，按编号顺序运行即可。建议从 `01_train_waltzdb_classifier.ipynb` 开始，逐步执行。
- **安装与依赖**：依赖文件未明确列出（README 未说明），但 Python 包列表已给出，包括 `Bio`、`Levenshtein`、`scikit-learn`、`pandas`、`numpy`、`matplotlib`、`seaborn`、`statsmodels`、`pydeseq2`、`gseapy`、`umap` 等。部分本地模块（`iupred2a_lib`、`pyaaisc`、`intersect`）需自行获取。
- **输入数据**：共享数据表位于 `files/` 目录，包括 `dSAM_MPs_v_paper_v2_new_locs.pkl`、`hTMs_uniprot_v1.pkl`、`AF2_with_Genes.pkl` 等。外部数据包括 WALTZ-DB 2.0、AlphaFold 人类蛋白质组表、UniProt、hyperLOPIT、BioGRID 等。
- **输出格式**：各 notebook 输出图表（PNG/PDF）和统计结果，具体格式因 notebook 而异。
- **GPU 需求**：README 未说明，但大部分分析为 CPU 密集型，仅 ESM 嵌入可能需 GPU（可选）。
- **调试入口**：每个 notebook 的 cell 均可独立运行，`FIGURE_MAP.csv` 提供了面板到 cell 的映射，便于定位和调试。

## 核心 idea

核心方法学洞察在于：将无序区中的短肽基序（6-9 个残基）视为潜在的“自组装代码”，通过监督学习（随机森林）从已知淀粉样六肽数据中学习 β-strand 介导的聚集倾向，再结合结构预测（AlphaFold pLDDT）和拓扑约束（膜蛋白、非螺旋、溶剂暴露）进行全蛋白质组筛选，从而发现一类新的、功能相关的自组装基序。其新颖性在于将无序区从“无结构”的被动区域重新定义为携带特定互作信息的活性模块，并通过多尺度验证建立了从序列到细胞功能的因果链。

## 可搬移点

- **随机森林分类器训练与评估**（`01_train_waltzdb_classifier.ipynb`）：可直接复用其训练流程、特征工程（one-hot 编码 + β-strand 能量）和评估指标（ROC、F1），用于其他 IDR 基序预测任务。
- **无序区判定逻辑**（基于 AlphaFold pLDDT < 70 的阈值）：可提取为独立函数，用于自定义 IDR 注释流程。
- **序列空间嵌入与聚类**（`06_mdsam_sequence_space_embedding.ipynb`）：其物理化学特征嵌入、GMM 聚类和关键字富集方法可迁移到其他 IDR 序列功能分析。
- **dSTORM 聚类分析**（`16_dstorm_htr7_cluster_analysis.ipynb`）：Voronoi 阈值化和 HDBSCAN 聚类流程可用于分析膜蛋白纳米尺度组织。
- **ESM 嵌入保守性分析**（`21_conservation_esm_embedding.ipynb`）：展示了如何用蛋白质语言模型嵌入进行无比对保守性评估，可直接用于 IDR 功能位点预测。
- **License**：README 未明确说明，需确认。

# mdSAM: Discovery of self-assembly motifs regulating membrane-protein organization and function

Analysis notebooks and figure panels for the manuscript *Discovery of self-assembly motifs regulating membrane-protein organization and function* (Elazar, Trivedi, et al., Babu lab, St. Jude Children's Research Hospital).

## Abstract

While cell-surface clustering of membrane proteins is central to numerous processes, its molecular determinants remain elusive. We postulated that peptide motifs within disordered regions of transmembrane proteins may drive self-association and clustering and developed an approach to identify them. Analysis of the human proteome revealed that one-fifth of membrane proteins (945 proteins; >1,400 motifs), including receptors and transporters, contain motifs that we term mdSAMs (membrane-disordered Self-Assembly Motifs). Biophysical, biochemical, structural, and cell-based analyses of mdSAMs in model and native membrane proteins demonstrate that mdSAMs can drive self-assembly and clustering. In the serotonin receptor HTR7, a single mdSAM-disrupting substitution alters nanoscale organization, attenuates basal and agonist-induced signaling, and shifts the transcriptional state of the cell. Notably, mdSAM sequences are unique, which might enable discrimination of self from non‑self during self‑assembly, yet conserved among orthologs, underscoring their relevance. These findings reveal a widespread mechanism linking membrane-protein self-assembly to cell-surface organization and function.

## What is an mdSAM?

An **mdSAM** (membrane-disordered Self-Assembly Motif) is a short peptide motif, usually 7-9 residues (median 8), located in an intrinsically disordered, solvent-exposed region of a transmembrane protein, that is predicted to self-assemble through beta-strand-mediated, amyloid-like interactions. The working hypothesis is that mdSAMs provide weak, sequence-specific self-association that can cluster membrane proteins at the cell surface.

**How mdSAMs are identified**

1. A random-forest classifier is trained on WALTZ-DB 2.0 (1,402 hexapeptides: 510 amyloid-forming, 892 non-forming) using the one-hot-encoded hexapeptide sequence plus the summed beta-strand free energy (F1 = 0.77, stratified 5-fold cross-validation).
2. Every hexapeptide window in human membrane proteins is scored; positive windows are Self-Assembly Motifs (SAMs).
3. A SAM is called an mdSAM if it lies in a disordered region: AlphaFold pLDDT < 70, non-helical and solvent exposed, excluding transmembrane segments and signal peptides. A ROC-derived threshold on consecutive positive windows sets the high-confidence set (Fig. S1I).

**What was found.** 1,425 high-confidence mdSAMs in 945 membrane proteins (about 20% of the 4,886 human membrane proteins analysed), 91% of them in N- or C-terminal tails, and 72% of mdSAM-containing proteins carry a single motif. Of 44 synthesised mdSAM peptides, 36 (81%) gave Thioflavin-T signal above buffer; in the eight peptides tested, proline substitutions reduced the signal, abolishing it in seven; cryo-EM showed ordered fibrils. In cells, mdSAMs increase surface puncta density of a synthetic scaffold and of native full-length proteins. In the serotonin receptor HTR7, the V451P substitution in the C-terminal mdSAM (VSVWVLQS) changes nanoscale cluster organisation, lowers basal and agonist-induced cAMP signalling (Emax reduced by 25%) and shifts the transcriptional state of the cell. mdSAM sequences are diverse and unique, and conserved among orthologs.

> Naming: older notebooks call these motifs **dSAM** (disordered SAM) and refer to the structured-region counterpart as **mSAM/sSAM/msSAM**. dSAM in a file name or variable means mdSAM.

## Repository contents

```
notebooks/   the 23 analysis notebooks listed below, numbered in pipeline order (outputs cleared)
files/       shared input tables read by the notebooks (see files/README.md)
FIGURE_MAP.csv   machine-readable map: paper panel -> notebook -> cell
```

## What each notebook does

Cell numbers are 0-based indices into the notebook (as in the `cells` list of the `.ipynb`).

### Data preparation and classifier

| Notebook | Task | Paper panels |
|---|---|---|
| `01_train_waltzdb_classifier.ipynb` | Trains and evaluates the random-forest classifier on WALTZ-DB 2.0 hexapeptides (one-hot sequence + summed beta-strand energy); reports test-set counts, stratified K-fold ROC and the beta-strand energy distributions. Saves the trained model. | Fig 1D; S1E-G |
| `02_alphafold_residue_table_and_early_plots.ipynb` | Builds the shared AlphaFold-derived residue table (`AF2_with_ENSG.pkl`, cell 205) used by most other notebooks; remaining cells hold earlier versions of exploratory plots. | (input table) |
| `03_mdsam_sequence_logos.ipynb` | Sequence logos and composition of mdSAMs and SAMs in membrane proteins (logomaker); also builds `hTMs_uniprot_v1.pkl` and `AF_IDR_v3.pkl`. Contains additional gnomAD analyses that are not part of the paper figures. | S1H |

### Discovery and diversity (Figs 1-2, S1-S2)

| Notebook | Task | Paper panels |
|---|---|---|
| `04_pasta_aggregation_comparison.ipynb` | Compares mdSAM predictions with PASTA energies and an aggregation threshold on windows around WALTZ-DB hexapeptides; ROC for the number of consecutive positive windows. | S1I-J |
| `05_uniprot_keyword_enrichment.ipynb` | UniProt keyword enrichment (observed minus expected, FDR) for mdSAM-containing membrane proteins: biological process, molecular function, disease. | Fig 1G; S1K |
| `06_mdsam_sequence_space_embedding.ipynb` | Embeds the mdSAM sequence space from physicochemical features, colours it by composition, clusters it (GMM) with keyword enrichment, draws the charge-archetype ternary plot, the dot matrix of mdSAM-containing proteins and the pairwise Levenshtein-distance analysis. | Fig 1F, 2F-I, 3A; S2E-G |
| `07_hyperlopit_organelle_enrichment.ipynb` | Re-analyses the hyperLOPIT subcellular fractionation (U2OS): fraction profiles, t-SNE and Gaussian-mixture organelle assignment, and mdSAM enrichment per organelle. | Fig 2A; S2A-C |

## Running the notebooks

The notebooks are distributed with their outputs cleared.

The notebooks were written for an interactive session and read three shared tables from `files/` (`dSAM_MPs_v_paper_v2_new_locs.pkl`, `hTMs_uniprot_v1.pkl`, `AF2_with_ENSG.pkl`); see `files/README.md`. Run each notebook with `notebooks/` as the working directory. Some notebooks still read other intermediate files that are not in this repository. Public inputs are WALTZ-DB 2.0, the AlphaFold human-proteome table of N. Davey (github.com/normandavey/ProcessedAlphafold), UniProt, the hyperLOPIT data (Thul et al., 2017), BioGRID 4.4.x, PANTHER 17 and GTEx v8. Supplementary data files accompany the paper.

Python packages imported by these notebooks (pip names can differ from import names): `Bio`, `Levenshtein`, `PIL`, `PyPDF2`, `adjustText`, `bokeh`, `cmasher`, `fcsparser`, `geopandas`, `gseapy`, `holoviews`, `intersect`, `iupred2a_lib`, `joblib`, `localcider`, `logomaker`, `matplotlib`, `matplotlib_venn`, `mycolorpy`, `networkx`, `numpy`, `pandas`, `plotly`, `pyaaisc`, `pycanal`, `pydeseq2`, `radialtree`, `rdfpy`, `ripleyk`, `sanbomics`, `scanpy`, `scipy`, `seaborn`, `shapely`, `sklearn`, `statsmodels`, `ternary`, `tqdm`, `umap`, `uncertainties`, `upsetplot`. `iupred2a_lib`, `pyaaisc` and `intersect` are local modules rather than PyPI packages.

one_liner: 该仓库提供ELF3无序结构域相分离与凝聚体分子动力学模拟的分析脚本和数据，聚焦IDP相分离场景，但互作机制建模深度有限。
card:
## 是什么

这是一个用于生成论文《Molecular basis of polyglutamine-modulated ELF3 phase change in Arabidopsis temperature response》中图表的 Python 脚本集合。仓库按三个子目录组织，分别对应 ELF3 蛋白 PrD（富含脯氨酸结构域）的三种模拟数据：HCG（层级链增长系综）、REST2（副本交换溶质温度标度模拟）和 Martini 粗粒化凝聚体轨迹。它主要用于分析固有无序蛋白（IDP）的构象系综、相分离行为以及多聚谷氨酰胺（polyQ）长度对温度响应的影响。

## 亮点

- **针对 IDP 模拟数据的专门分析**：脚本直接处理分子动力学模拟输出，提取回旋半径、二级结构、残基间距离、溶剂可及表面积等关键物理量。
- **多尺度覆盖**：从原子级 REST2 模拟到粗粒化 Martini 凝聚体模拟，提供从单链构象到多链相分离的完整分析链条。
- **数据可复现**：所有模拟数据公开托管在 Zenodo 和 Flatiron 服务器，脚本与数据一一对应，便于复现论文图表。
- **轻量级脚本**：每个脚本聚焦单一分析任务，易于阅读、修改和扩展。

## 为何对本课题有用

该仓库直接针对 IDR/IDP 与相分离（LLPS）的交叉领域，具体价值包括：
- **构象系综分析**：HCG 和 REST2 脚本提供了从模拟轨迹中计算系综平均性质（如 Rg、二级结构倾向）的现成代码，可直接用于其他 IDP 的构象分析。
- **polyQ 调控机制**：通过比较不同 polyQ 长度（0Q、3Q、7Q）的模拟数据，揭示了 polyQ 如何调节 ELF3 的温度响应相变，为理解 polyQ 在 IDP 互作中的作用提供方法学参考。
- **相分离互作建模**：Martini 凝聚体脚本分析蛋白-水相互作用和凝聚体内部距离，为研究 IDP 驱动的相分离提供分析模板。
- **可迁移的分析流程**：脚本中的 KDE 绘图、距离分布、螺旋倾向等分析逻辑可迁移至其他 IDP 模拟数据。

## 怎么用

- **主入口**：无统一主程序，每个脚本独立运行，例如 `python HCG/rg_hcg.py` 或 `python REST2/rg.py`。
- **安装与依赖**：依赖 Python 3 及常见科学计算库（如 NumPy、Matplotlib、SciPy、MDTraj 等），具体依赖未在 README 中列出，需查看脚本头部 import 语句。
- **输入数据**：需要从指定 URL 下载模拟轨迹文件（HCG 数据、REST2 轨迹、Martini 轨迹），格式可能为 .xtc、.pdb 等，具体格式需查看脚本。
- **输出**：生成图表（如 PDF/PNG）和数值结果，用于论文插图。
- **GPU 需求**：不需要 GPU，纯 CPU 分析即可。
- **调试示例**：每个脚本自带数据路径，可直接运行复现论文图表，适合断点调试。

## 核心 idea

核心方法学在于**将分子动力学模拟轨迹转化为可解释的物理化学描述**：通过计算 Rg、二级结构、残基间距离等序参量，量化 polyQ 长度对 ELF3-PrD 构象系综和相分离行为的影响，从而建立序列-构象-相行为之间的联系。其可借鉴之处在于**系统化的系综分析流程**，而非单一算法创新。

## 可搬移点

- **Rg 和二级结构分析脚本**（如 `REST2/rg.py`、`REST2/ss_0Q_helix_per_res.py`）：可直接移植到其他 IDP 模拟分析中，只需修改轨迹读取路径。
- **距离分布和 KDE 绘图脚本**（如 `REST2/dist_f527_haro.py`、`REST2/kde_plot_haro_rg.py`）：提供现成的分布比较和可视化模板。
- **凝聚体分析脚本**（如 `Condensates/protein_water_interactions_300K.py`）：可迁移至其他相分离模拟分析。
- **License**：未在 README 中说明，需确认。

# ELF3 Python Analysis Scripts
A place to store code used to generate figures for the publication, "Molecular basis of polyglutamine-modulated ELF3 phase change in Arabidopsis temperature response."

# Contents
# HCG:
Contains python scripts and data used to generate figures pertaining to ELF3-PrD hierarchical chain growth ensembles.

# REST2:
Contains scripts and data needed to create figures pertaining to ELF3-PrD REST2 simulation data.

# Condensates:
Contains scripts and data used to generate some of the figures pertaining to Martini trajectories.

# Data available at ELF3 Project Website:
https://www.simonsfoundation.org/molecular-dynamics-simulations-of-intrinsically-disordered-proteins/

HCG data: https://users.flatironinstitute.org/~shanson/elf3prd_hcg.zip

REST2 trajectories: https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.13226984

Martini trajectories: https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.13285376

## 是什么
BENDER 是一个面向固有无序蛋白（IDP）的粗粒化（coarse-grained）构象系综数据集与配套分析/复现代码仓库。它提供了 10,282 条来自六个生物类群（哺乳动物、真菌、植物、原生生物、细菌、病毒）的全长无序蛋白序列，使用 CALVADOS-2 和 MPIPI-Recharged 两种粗粒化力场进行分子动力学模拟，并附带将轨迹转化为每序列性质（如 Flory 指数、接触图、SAXS 对比等）的分析管线，以及生成论文全部图表的脚本。

## 亮点
- **大规模、跨物种的 IDP 构象系综**：覆盖 10,282 条序列，远超一般 IDP 数据集规模，且明确标注物种来源，便于进化视角分析。
- **多力场对比**：同一序列用 CALVADOS-2 和 MPIPI-Recharged（部分用 MPIPI-GG）模拟，直接支持力场间分歧的系统性比较。
- **高度可复现**：所有图表脚本从 `data/` 读取即可生成与论文像素级一致的图，环境依赖完整（`environment.yml`）。
- **模块化分析管线**：`analysis/` 下按力场分目录，共享规则集中在 `bender_common.py`，便于扩展或替换。
- **数据与代码分离**：轨迹存储在 Hugging Face，本地只保留每序列性质表，降低仓库体积。

## 为何对本课题有用
BENDER 直接针对 IDP 构象系综的粗粒化模拟与分析，与课题高度对齐：
- **力场评估与选择**：提供了两种主流粗粒化力场（CALVADOS-2、MPIPI-Recharged）在大量 IDP 上的表现对比，可用于指导 IDP 模拟中力场的选择或参数调整。
- **构象系综分析**：`bender_common.py` 中的 Flory 拟合、接触图、链解缠绕等逻辑，可直接复用于自定义 IDP 系综分析。
- **无序性验证**：包含与 AlphaFold2 PAE 的一致性检查，可用于验证预测的无序区域。
- **互作相关**：论文主题“精氨酸-芳香族吸引”涉及 IDP 内残基互作，其接触图分析可迁移到 IDP 与配体/其他蛋白互作的研究。
- **跨物种比较**：六类生物的序列覆盖，支持研究 IDP 序列-构象关系的进化差异。

## 怎么用
- **安装**：`conda env create -f environment.yml`，激活 `bender` 环境。模拟还需额外安装 CALVADOS、OpenMpipi（pip 源码安装）和 LAMMPS（仅 MPIPI-GG）。
- **复现图表**：进入 `figures/source/`，运行如 `python make_fig1_overview.py`，输出到 `output/`。需先设置环境变量（如 `BENDER_DATA`、`BENDER_OUT`）。
- **重新计算性质**：需从 Hugging Face 下载轨迹，设置 `BENDER_TRAJ` 和 `BENDER_WORK`，运行如 `python analysis/traj_analysis_calvados_v2.py run --graph --workers 8 --out work/calvados2_300K`。
- **运行模拟**：`simulations/` 下按力场提供 SLURM 提交脚本，输入序列在 `data/sequences/bender_10282.fasta`。
- **测试**：`analysis/tests/test_reference.py` 提供对共享规则的参考检查，可作调试入口。
- **数据格式**：输入为 FASTA 序列；输出为 CSV 表格（每序列性质）、接触图（可能为 numpy 数组）、SAXS 曲线（需从 SASBDB 下载）。
- **GPU 需求**：模拟和大部分分析基于 CPU（OpenMM/LAMMPS），无需 GPU；但若使用 metapredict（pip 依赖）进行无序预测，可能受益于 GPU，但非必需。

## 核心 idea
BENDER 的核心方法学在于**通过大规模、跨物种的 IDP 粗粒化模拟，系统性地揭示不同力场在残基互作（如精氨酸-芳香族吸引）上的分歧，从而将力场差异与序列组成和进化背景关联起来**。其可复用的洞察是：利用统一的轨迹分析框架（`bender_common.py`）提取每序列的物理性质（如 Flory 指数、接触偏好），使得力场间的比较和生物学解释成为可能。

## 可搬移点
- **`analysis/bender_common.py`**：包含帧选择、链解缠绕、Flory 拟合、接触计算等核心逻辑，可解耦后直接 import 进自定义 IDP 系综分析管线。
- **`analysis/sequence_descriptors.py`**：序列特征计算（如电荷、疏水性），可用于 IDP 序列-构象关系建模。
- **`analysis/saxs/validate_saxs_constructs.py`**：SAXS 对比逻辑，可迁移到 IDP 实验-模拟验证。
- **`analysis/validation/pae_v2.py`**：与 AlphaFold2 PAE 的一致性检查，可用于无序预测验证。
- **`simulations/calvados2/prepare.py`**：粗粒化模拟输入准备脚本，可适配其他 IDP 序列。
- **License**：代码 MIT，数据 CC BY 4.0，允许自由使用和修改，但需确认引用要求。
readme:
# BENDER

Code and per-sequence data for **"Arginine–Aromatic Attraction Divides Coarse-Grained IDP Force Fields Across the Tree of Life"**
(T. Rahman, submitted to the *Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation*).

BENDER holds coarse-grained ensembles of 10,282 fully disordered proteins from six taxa (mammals, fungi,
plants, protists, bacteria and viruses), simulated with CALVADOS-2 and MPIPI-Recharged, with a 957-sequence subset
also simulated with MPIPI-GG. This repository contains the simulation inputs and run scripts, the analysis code that
turns trajectories into per-sequence properties, the per-sequence tables themselves and the scripts that draw every
figure and generated table of the paper.

## Data

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Per-sequence properties, force-field agreement, PAE agreement, disorder checks, SAXS benchmark | `data/` in this repository (see `data/README.md`) |
| CALVADOS-2 trajectories (300 K) | [huggingface.co/datasets/taseef/BENDER](https://huggingface.co/datasets/taseef/BENDER) |
| MPIPI-Recharged trajectories (300 K) | [huggingface.co/datasets/taseef/MPIPI-Recharged](https://huggingface.co/datasets/taseef/MPIPI-Recharged) |
| MPIPI-GG trajectories and the per-sequence properties of both MPIPI models | [huggingface.co/datasets/taseef/BENDER-MPIPI](https://huggingface.co/datasets/taseef/BENDER-MPIPI) |

Sequences are distributed with the data because many of the UniProt accessions have since become obsolete.

## Layout

```
paths.py              every input and output location (override with environment variables, see below)
data/                 per-sequence tables used by the paper
simulations/          inputs and run scripts
  calvados2/            CALVADOS-2 (prepare.py, SLURM submitter)
  mpipi_recharged/      MPIPI-Recharged with OpenMpipi in OpenMM
  mpipi_gg/             MPIPI-GG with LAMMPS
  controls/             hnRNPA1 variants, termini and histidine controls, parameter swaps (see its README)
  inputs/               FASTA and TSV inputs of the control and swap sets
analysis/             trajectories to per-sequence properties
  bender_common.py      shared rules: frame selection, chain unwrapping, Flory fits, contacts
  traj_analysis_calvados_v2.py, mpipi/, mpipi_recharged/   per-force-field pipelines
  validation/           agreement with AlphaFold2 PAE and between force fields
  saxs/                 SAXS benchmark (77 constructs)
  tables/               assembly of the per-sequence tables, NCBI taxonomy check
  tests/                reference checks on two bundled trajectories
figures/source/       one script per figure or generated table
flory_axis_letter/    code of the Flory-axis letter (see its README)
```

## Reproducing the figures

The figure scripts read only `data/` and write to `output/`:

```bash
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate bender
cd figures/source
python make_fig1_overview.py
```

| Figure | Script |
|---|---|
| TOC graphic | `make_toc_ring.py` |
| Fig. 1, BENDER from one protein to the dataset | `make_fig1_overview.py` |
| Fig. 2, cross-force-field disagreement | `make_fig_disagreement.py` |
| Fig. 3, residue-pair B2 mechanism | `make_fig_b2_mechanism.py` |
| Fig. 4, taxa | `make_fig_lineages.py` |
| Fig. 5, parameter swaps and hnRNPA1 variants | `make_fig_tests.py` |
| Fig. 6, chain length | `make_fig_length.py` |
| SI, taxonomic composition | `make_supp_species_sunburst.py` |
| SI, disorder checks | `make_supp_disorder.py`, `make_supp_disorder_tables.py` |
| SI, AlphaFold2 PAE agreement | `make_fig3_pae_validation.py` |
| SI, property distributions and Flory fits | `make_supp_distributions.py` |
| SI, SAXS benchmark and Kratky profiles | `make_supp_saxs_f4p.py plot` |
| SI, Gly/Ser/Pro swap on the SAXS benchmark | `make_fig_saxs_swap.py` |
| SI tables of the swaps and hnRNPA1 variants | `make_supp_tests_tables.py` |
| Numbers quoted in the text | `paper_numbers_recharged.py` |

Run from this repository, every figure above is pixel-identical to the one in the paper. The Kratky profiles also
need the experimental SAXS curves, which are not redistributed here. Download them from
[SASBDB](https://www.sasbdb.org) as `<SASBDB code>.dat` (codes in `data/saxs/traj_vs_saxs_rg.csv`) into
`data/saxs/sasbdb/`, or point `BENDER_SASBDB` at them.

## Flory-axis letter

`flory_axis_letter/` holds the code of a second paper built on BENDER, "Taking Charge across the Tree of Life: Universal Flory Scaling of Intrinsically Disordered Proteins" (T. Rahman and V. N. Uversky). It runs from `data/` with
`bash flory_axis_letter/run_all.sh`; see `flory_axis_letter/README.md`.

## Recomputing the tables from trajectories

The analysis scripts need the trajectories, laid out under `trajectories/` as described in `paths.py`. Set
`BENDER_TRAJ` if they are elsewhere, and `BENDER_WORK` for intermediate outputs (per-frame features and contact maps).
For example, CALVADOS-2 properties at 300 K come from

```bash
python analysis/traj_analysis_calvados_v2.py run --graph --workers 8 --out work/calvados2_300K
```

and MPIPI-Recharged properties from `analysis/mpipi_recharged/recharged_nu.py` and `recharged_300K_features.py`.
`analysis/tests/test_reference.py` checks the shared rules against two bundled reference trajectories.

## Running simulations

`simulations/` holds the scripts as run on a SLURM cluster (USF GAIVI). The full sequence set is
`data/sequences/bender_10282.fasta`. Output roots default to `~/bender_runs/` and can be changed with `--outdir`,
`--outroot` or the variables named in each submitter.

| Force field | Software | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| CALVADOS-2 | [CALVADOS](https://github.com/KULL-Centre/CALVADOS) in OpenMM (`prepare.py` predates release 0.9, which rejects its `runtime = 0` setting) | Tesei and Lindorff-Larsen, *Open Res. Eur.* 2023 |
| MPIPI-Recharged | OpenMpipi in OpenMM | R. Tejedor et al., *ACS Cent. Sci.* 2025 |
| MPIPI-GG | LAMMPS | Joseph et al., *Nat. Comput. Sci.* 2021; Lotthammer et al., *Nat. Methods* 2024 |

## Environment variables

| Variable | Default | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `BENDER_DATA` | `data/` | per-sequence tables |
| `BENDER_OUT` | `output/` | figures and generated tables |
| `BENDER_TRAJ` | `trajectories/` | trajectories from Hugging Face |
| `BENDER_WORK` | `work/` | intermediate outputs of the trajectory analyses |
| `BENDER_SASBDB` | `data/saxs/sasbdb/` | experimental SAXS profiles |

## License

Code is released under the MIT License (`LICENSE`). The data in `data/` are released under CC BY 4.0, as on
Hugging Face.

## Citation

T. Rahman, Arginine–Aromatic Attraction Divides Coarse-Grained IDP Force Fields Across the Tree of Life, submitted to *J. Chem. Theory
Comput.* (2026).
